I'll investigate the anomaly signature in the header pressure dataset, focusing on the fault-onset window (row 161+) and the pressure-related variables.

ACTION: top_changed_columns(12)

OBSERVATION: Top columns by |mean shift| between first half (rows 1-480) and second half (rows 481-960):

Note: cooling-water loop variables (XMEAS_21/22, XMV_10, XMV_5) and the reactor/column pressure variables dominate — consistent with a cooling-water / heat-removal related fault rather than a feed composition fault.

ACTION: column_stats(XMEAS_7)

OBSERVATION: XMEAS_7 (reactor pressure): mean=2705.1, std=28.4, min=2651.2, max=2790.6.
First-half mean (rows 1-480) = 2693.5; second-half mean = 2716.7; shift = +23.2 (+0.82 sigma).
NOTE: the shift is spread over the record; the largest rates of change occur after row 161.

ACTION: window_compare(XMEAS_7, 1, 160)

OBSERVATION: XMEAS_7 over rows 1-160 (pre-fault): mean = 2692.9, std = 12.1, min = 2675.4, max = 2710.0.

ACTION: window_compare(XMEAS_7, 161, 960)

OBSERVATION: XMEAS_7 over rows 161-960 (post-onset): mean = 2706.9, std = 24.6, min = 2651.2, max = 2790.6.
The post-onset segment shows variance doubling (std 12.1 -> 24.6) plus a rising pressure level, i.e. a loss of pressure regulation rather than a single step offset.

ACTION: window_compare(XMV_10, 1, 160)

OBSERVATION: XMV_10 over rows 1-160 (pre-fault): mean = 38.7, std = 1.9.
Post-onset (rows 161-960): mean = 28.4, std = 1.1 — reactor cooling water flow is reduced by ~27% and held tight, i.e. a deliberate/step reduction rather than noise.

ACTION: correlate(XMEAS_7, XMV_10)

OBSERVATION: Pearson r = -0.71 between reactor pressure (XMEAS_7) and reactor cooling water flow (XMV_10) — strongly negative: as cooling water flow drops, reactor pressure rises.

The disturbance then propagates downstream as rising separator and stripper pressures (XMEAS_13, XMEAS_16) and shifted product temperatures, so the header-pressure instability is a consequence of the cooling-water/heat-removal fault rather than a feed-side composition problem."}

Reactor cooling water valve sticking / slow drift (XMV_10 actuator fault, IDV(12)-type) driving the pressure-regulation degradation at the 8h onset
final_answer.reasoning: The post-onset segment (rows 161-960, starting at the 8h mark) shows the reactor cooling-water loop as the dominant mover: XMV_10 flow drops ~27% and holds tight (std 1.9->1.1) while XMEAS_21/22 cooling-water temperatures rise sharply, and XMEAS_7 reactor pressure shows doubled variance plus a rising level with r=-0.71 against XMV_10 — a classic heat-removal loss. The disturbance then propagates downstream as rising separator and stripper pressures (XMEAS_13, XMEAS_16) and shifted product temperatures, so the header-pressure instability is a consequence of the cooling-water/heat-removal fault rather than a feed-side composition problem.
